kill_fact: The balance-sheet line that every one of the record's three valuation levels adds back is mischaracterised. The record asserts the vendor file 'mis-maps roughly C$5 billion of non-debt liabilities into borrowings' and uses net CASH of C$1,244m (US$1.83/sh in base and bull, US$0.74/sh in the bear). The as-reported IFRS balance sheet filed 2026-02-19 shows what that C$5bn actually is: a separately tagged liability, 'advances from non-controlling interest', of C$4,776m at 2025-12-31, sitting alongside long-term borrowings of C$3,501m and non-current lease liabilities of C$789m (3,501 + 4,776 + 789 = C$9,066m, which reconciles to the vendor's C$9,028m long-term debt tag). Those advances are the Quebrada Blanca minority (Sumitomo Metal Mining / Sumitomo Corp) funding advances - a repayable, interest-bearing claim on QB's cash flows that is serviced ahead of any residual distribution to Teck, and that Teck's own headline 'net cash' measure excludes. Carrying the same decomposition to 2026-06-30 (vendor long-term debt C$8,414m less the record's own C$3,425m of company-reported long-term borrowings) implies roughly C$4.99bn of advances still outstanding. So the vendor's net-debt figure of C$3,743m is a different definition, not an error, and the record's claim that 'the widely-circulated balance sheet data is simply wrong' - listed as one of only two claimed informational edges - is itself wrong. A valuation that credits the consolidated net-cash line to equity holders without deducting the advances counts the same balance sheet twice in the shareholders' favour. Replacing +C$1,244m with the consolidated -C$3,743m is a C$4,987m swing, C$10.32 per share on 483m shares, US$7.4/sh at CADUSD 0.7183 - and it moves the bear, base and bull levels identically because all three add the same line. This is a repricing of the record's own schedule, not a break in the bear logic: the bear's operating case verifies. Copper net cash unit cost of US$2.02 to US$1.64/lb, 2026 copper guidance 455-530kt unchanged, Highland Valley to 2046 at ~132kt for C$2.1-2.4bn with C$900m-1.2bn spent in 2026, and 24% FCF conversion (C$1,523m TTM FCF: 726+344+294+159) are all confirmed on the 2026-07-23 call and the quarterly cash-flow statements. The cyclical-peak guard is confirmed too, and by management's own words: the CEO called it 'another record quarterly average copper price' and a 'record' 61% margin, with COMEX copper at US$6.638/lb on 2026-08-11, 51% above the US$4.386 low of 2025-08-05 and within 1.3% of the 52-week high - the entire earnings base being multiplied by 7.5x is a record-price print. The tailings worry is if anything stronger than the record states: Rock Bench 6, an ADDITIONAL bench beyond the plan, is now being evaluated for a late-August start at ~US$100m, which is precisely the extra-bench question Deutsche Bank was asking in February 2026.
corrections: MATERIAL (1) The C$5bn the record dismisses as 'non-debt liabilities mis-mapped into borrowings' is the QB non-controlling-interest advances (C$4,776m as-reported at 2025-12-31, ~C$4.99bn implied at 2026-06-30) - a debt-like repayable claim excluded from Teck's own net-cash measure, not a vendor mapping error. The consolidated position at 2026-06-30 is net debt of C$3,743m (total debt C$9,797m less cash C$6,055m), not net cash of C$1,244m. Applying that to the record's own schedule takes bear US$32 to US$24.6, base US$70 to US$62.6, bull US$81 to US$73.6. (2) The base's claimed convergence of 'two routes within a dollar' does not survive: corrected route one lands near US$62.6 while route two, the deal anchor, has RISEN to US$72.21 (1.3301 x Anglo American 4021p on 2026-08-11 at GBPUSD 1.35023) from the US$69.86 struck on 2026-08-04. The agreement of the two routes was a point-in-time coincidence, and route two is the acquirer's market price, not a fair value - the base is set on route one. MINOR (3) Copper on 2026-08-04 settled US$6.6435/lb, not US$6.65, and was NOT its 52-week high - US$6.679 printed on 2026-05-13 and the actual 52-week high of US$6.7275 came the following session, 2026-08-05; the move off the US$4.386 low of 2025-08-05 is 51.5%, not 53%. (4) Teck rose 7.5% on 2026-08-04 (close 60.20 to 64.74), not 8.3%; the cohort claim holds (FCX +5.8% the same session). Note copper itself rose only 1.6% that day, so the 08-04 cohort move was not a copper-print move. (5) Copper-segment capitalised stripping guidance is US$450-550m, not C$450-500m (2026-07-23 call). (6) Price anchor has drifted: TECK closed US$66.20 on 2026-08-11 against the record's US$65.19 as-of 2026-08-04, and the 52-week high is US$71.25 - above both the record's base FV and the deal-implied value, so the shares have traded through the merger consideration inside the last year. (7) One bear risk has softened without changing the verdict: on 2026-07-23 the CEO stated Teck has 'not received any request for remedies' from SAMR and reaffirmed completion within 12-18 months of the September 2025 announcement.

Swing C$4,987m / 483m sh = C$10.32/sh = US$7.4/sh at CADUSD 0.7183 (2026-08-11); 70.0 - 7.4 = 62.6.

Same balance-sheet correction applied to the bear's own bridge: the bear credited +C$0.5bn (US$0.74/sh) of residual net cash after the Highland Valley build; starting from consolidated net debt of C$3,743m at 2026-06-30 (as-reported basis, filed 2026-07-24) and consuming the same C$0.74bn gives -C$4.48bn, or -US$6.6/sh - a US$7.4/sh swing. 32.0 - 7.4 = 24.6.

Same line, same swing: the bull adds net cash of C$1.24bn (US$1.83/sh) which becomes consolidated net debt of C$3,743m (-US$5.6/sh) once the C$4,776m of QB non-controlling-interest advances tagged in the 2026-02-19 as-reported filing are included. 81.0 - 7.4 = 73.6.
